facts.statement: Nambalia is classified as a basal sauropodomorph dinosaur.
facts.quote: Nambalia is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur.

facts.statement: Nambalia lived in what is now Telangana, central India, during the Late Triassic period from the late Norian to the earliest Rhaetian.
facts.quote: It lived during the Late Triassic period (late Norian to earliest Rhaetian) in what is now Telangana, central India.

facts.statement: The fossils were discovered in the Upper Maleri Formation within the Pranhita–Godavari Basin, north of Nambal village.
facts.quote: ISI R273 was discovered and collected from the Upper Maleri Formation within the Pranhita–Godavari Basin, north of Nambal village.

facts.statement: Nambalia was first named by Fernando E. Novas, Martin D. Ezcurra, Sankar Chatterjee, and T. S. Kutty in 2011, with the type species Nambalia roychowdhurii.
facts.quote: It was first named by Fernando E. Novas, Martin D. Ezcurra, Sankar Chatterjee and T. S. Kutty in 2011 and the type species is Nambalia roychowdhurii.

facts.statement: The generic name Nambalia is derived from the Indian village of Nambal near the type locality.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Indian village of Nambal which is close to the type locality.

facts.statement: The specific name roychowdhurii honors Dr. Roy Chowdhuri for his research on Triassic vertebrate faunas of India.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Dr. Roy Chowdhuri, for his research on the Triassic vertebrate faunas of India.

facts.statement: Nambalia belongs to the parent group Sauropodomorpha.
Nambalia is classified within the class Saurischia.
Nambalia lived between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago during the Norian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus is known from a holotype consisting of partially articulated postcranial material and paratypes representing at least two individuals of different sizes found closely associated.
rejected.quote: It is known from the holotype ISI R273, parts 1–3, partially articulated postcranial material and from the paratypes ISI R273, parts 4-29, including partial postcrania of at least two individuals of different sizes found closely associated and one of them is nearly the same size as the holotype.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'at least two individuals of different sizes found'

rejected.statement: Cladistic analysis places Nambalia as basal to Efraasia, Plateosauravus, Ruehleia, and Plateosauria, but more derived than Thecodontosaurus, Pantydraco, and Guaibasauridae.
rejected.quote: A cladistic analysis by Novas et al. found that Nambalia is basal to Efraasia, Plateosauravus, Ruehleia and Plateosauria, but more derived than Thecodontosaurus, Pantydraco, and Guaibasauridae.
